fixes.what: {"region": "Liaoxi"} resolves to 365 cells (the gazetteer defines it as Liaoning minus the Liaodong polygon), 110 of them north and east of the Liao River (Kaiyuan, Xifeng, Changtu), so the minus-Liaoxi corrections cut Jin land held since 1619 out of the 1626-1628 and 1636-1641 shapes and the 1642 gain handed it over from the Ming a second time.
fixes.why: gazetteer resolve: Kaiyuan (124.04 E, 42.55 N) and Xifeng fall in Liaoxi, not in Liaodong; Cliopatria's own 1629 and 1632 shapes hold 59 and 85 of these cells; the Nurhaci page has Tieling 'in the summer of 1619' and Kaiyuan occupied in the same campaign. The dossier's own text calls Liaoxi 'the Guangning-Jinzhou-Songshan side of the Liao River'.

The Liaodong peninsula towns of 1621-1622 (confidence 1, date from Cliopatria); the Later Jin page's 'the entire eastern part of Liao[dong]' may date them to 1621.
End and terms of the 1627 invasion (confidence 1, bridged from the joseon dossier, which has infobox 'January - 3 March 1627').
Whether Ningyuan and the corridor to the Shanhai Pass (Xingcheng, Suizhong) stayed Ming until 1644; the 1642 gain gives all of western Liaoning.
The 1644 dissolve is a Cliopatria row boundary, not an event (confidence 1); the orchestrator should decide whether later-jin-dynasty and qing-dynasty are merged.

The 1636 Cliopatria shape (kept apart from Korea and Liaoxi) also holds Inner Mongolia west to 100.6 E (Ordos, part of Alxa), 89 cells of Gansu and Ningxia, 336 of northern Hebei and 14 of Mongolia; no opened page puts the Ordos or Alxa under the Jin in 1636 and the Gansu/Ningxia cells may overlap the Ming. Unflagged in the note.
Kaiyuan, occupied with Tieling in 1619 per the Nurhaci page (undated sentence), is outside the corrected 1619-1625 shapes (Cliopatria 1622 and the Liaodong polygon both stop south of it).
The eastern Inner Mongolian submissions before 1635 (Khorchin alliance 1624-1626, Kharachin 1628) are left out as associations; a vassal_start pair would show them.
